referees.quote: On the technical level, I don't have any significant concerns; the paper is worth publishing. However, I am unsure whether Nature Communications is the correct journal
I can in principle recommend publication provided that the authors can address my questions below. However, I want to point out that the manuscript is relatively weak in terms of novelty.
I would suggest publication in Nature Communications if the authors address the following comments

note: No transfer from another journal is indicated; Version 0 is the first round. No referee co-signed another's report. R2's first-round report appears as an attachment at the end of the file; the in-text remark says only 'See the attached report.' R1 is borderline: they find the paper technically sound and worth publishing but question its novelty and fit for the journal. They only ask the authors to highlight novelty, so this was read as minor revision rather than reject. R3 is borderline between minor and major revision: they call the quantum-geometry link 'somewhat tenuous' and ask for clearer explanation and a more critical discussion of assumptions and alternative mechanisms. These requests involve rewriting and discussion, not new data, and R3 frames them as conditions for publication, so this was read as minor revision. All three recommended publication in round 2.
